title: Woody Harrelson Turned Down Haymitch Twice
excerpt:
Harrelson initially worried the Hunger Games role offered too little to do.
Director Gary Ross changed his mind in a ten-minute phone call.
body_md:
Woody Harrelson revealed during a joint Vanity Fair interview with Joseph Zada that he rejected the role of Haymitch Abernathy twice before joining The Hunger Games. Zada, who portrays the younger Haymitch in Sunrise on the Reaping, was surprised by the admission.

Harrelson had read and enjoyed the novels, but felt the character might not offer enough for him to do as an actor. Looking back, he regards that approach to evaluating the part as misguided.

Director Gary Ross eventually called him personally, saying he had no second choice for the role. A conversation lasting around ten minutes persuaded Harrelson to accept. He now finds it difficult to imagine missing the experience and the relationships he developed through the franchise.

Ross directed the original 2012 film, with Francis Lawrence directing the subsequent installments and prequels. Sunrise on the Reaping explores young Haymitch's forced participation in the second Quarter Quell. Its cast also features McKenna Grace, Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons and Elle Fanning.

Harrelson returns briefly alongside Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson. Lawrence described the emotional experience of returning as Katniss and reuniting with familiar colleagues on Call Her Daddy. The film reportedly opened to approximately $120 million.
